newsitem.title: UK: British Gas investors set to agree demerger.
newsitem.headline: British Gas investors set to agree demerger.

text.p: Shareholders in British Gas, Britain's largest utility, will vote later on Wednesday on the company's proposed demerger, which would see its trading arm hived off from the transport business.
The new firm, Centrica, which will also hold the giant Morecambe Bay gas fields, faces the challenge of fighting increased competition as the British gas market is opened up to competition.
The market for big industrial users has already been liberalised, while the domestic market should see competition introduced across the country by 1998.

Centrica probably also wants to renegotiate more of the so-called take-or-pay contracts with North Sea gas producers. These long-term deals oblige British Gas to buy fixed amounts of gas at set prices even if cannot sell it on.
British Gas first announced its demerger plan a year ago with the aim of protecting the profitable pipeline transportation business from the take-or-pay burden.
The British Gas rump will not only include the pipeline network in the UK, but also British Gas' exploration and production activities abroad.
Shareholders will also have to vote on the plan to change the name of the remaining British Gas rump to BG Plc.
